title: Silas and the Cipher
premise: Cyrus Oyelaran, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, discovers that the diary of Marion Voss—a woman who vanished eleven years ago—contains entries written after her disappearance, in handwriting he slowly realizes is his own future hand, or someone imitating it. Following the diary's cipher through the cathedral's locked crypt and the town's sealed records, he learns that Marion faked her death to escape a powerful family whose patriarch, Aldous Greer, has been blackmailing half of Blackmere, and that a witness to Greer's original crime—rumored dead—survives in hiding. As the statute of limitations closes in, Cyrus must choose between the belonging he's found among the town's complicit, comfortable families and the truth that would burn it all down. In the end, Cyrus finds the witness, exposes Greer before the deadline, and chooses exile from Blackmere—but not before the town's outcasts, his true found family, choose to follow him.
about_author: Emrys Pemberton is the pen name of a former cathedral verger who spent a decade cataloguing parish records in northern England before turning to fiction. Their work explores the quiet violence of small towns and the archives that remember what people would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Absence
chapters.summary: Cyrus Oyelaran, POV. Establishes his ordered life among the cathedral archives, his ritual of cataloguing the town's secrets, and his loneliness beneath the routine. He mentions Marion Voss's missing-person file, untouched for eleven years. Emotional beat: the ache of a man who belongs to a building but not to a town.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. While re-shelving donations, he finds a diary donated anonymously—Marion Voss's—with entries continuing a year past her disappearance. The final entry is dated three weeks ago. He tells no one. Emotional beat: vertigo; the archive he trusted has just lied to him.

chapters.title: The Greer Pew
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. He investigates who donated the diary and notices the Greer family's names woven through Marion's final entries. A tense Sunday service where patriarch Aldous Greer watches him too closely. Emotional beat: first fear—the powerful are already aware of him.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. He picks the crypt's lock and finds Marion's research hidden in a sarcophagus: evidence Aldous Greer killed a business partner in 2013, and that Marion was the bookkeeper who found the ledger. A marginal note names a witness only as 'T.' Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of real knowledge.

chapters.title: Constable Iyer's Cold File
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Priya Iyer, the one police officer who never believed Marion's case was closed. Cyrus approaches her; she warns him the Greers own the town's institutions, including her superiors. Emotional beat: two lonely skeptics recognizing each other—the first spark of found family.

chapters.title: A Dinner with the Devil
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Aldous Greer invites him to dinner, offers him a funded archive expansion—bribery dressed as patronage—and mentions Marion's name with practiced grief. Cyrus accepts the money to buy time. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging to power, and self-disgust.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Stones
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Priya, alternating. They decode Marion's marginalia as a cipher keyed to the cathedral's carved saints, pointing to locations across Blackmere. Each site yields a piece of the original ledger. Emotional beat: partnership deepening into trust; the case becoming personal.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. He interviews townsfolk about 'T' and hits a wall of coordinated silence—until the old sexton, Wren, lets slip that the witness's funeral was closed-casket. Emotional beat: the horror of a town that has agreed, collectively, not to know.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren, POV (flashback-framed). Eleven years ago he helped stage the witness Tomas Ellery's death to save him from Greer, and has kept watch ever since. He refuses to reveal Tomas's location. Emotional beat: guilt worn smooth by a decade of silence.

chapters.title: The Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. A suspicious fire guts the archive annexe; the diary survives only because Cyrus had hidden it. He realizes Greer won't bribe anymore. Priya is suspended from the force. Emotional beat: loss, escalation, and the point of no return.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Is Worth
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Greer's lawyer reveals they know Cyrus's own buried secret—a falsified credential from his past—and offer silence in exchange for the diary. He almost takes it. Emotional beat: corruption as temptation; power buying men exactly like him.

chapters.title: The Outcasts' Table
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Cyrus finds refuge with the town's ignored people—Wren, the diner owner Odile, Priya, and the Greer estranged son, Miles—who have quietly shared suspicions for years. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing; for the first time, Cyrus is not alone.

chapters.title: Miles Greer's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Miles, POV. He confirms his father's crimes from inside the family and reveals Aldous keeps a private safe with the original ledger—and that the statute expires in nineteen days. Emotional beat: a son choosing truth over blood.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The group plans: obtain the ledger, find Tomas, and get sworn testimony before the deadline. Greer's men begin following Cyrus. Emotional beat: ticking-clock tension and the strange calm of commitment.

chapters.title: The Saint Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Re-examining the cipher, he realizes its final coordinate isn't a place in Blackmere but the cathedral itself—the witness has been hiding within the one building no one searches. Emotional beat: revelation; the archive's irony completing itself.

chapters.title: Tomas Ellery, Alive
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. In the crypt's sealed passage, Cyrus finds Tomas—disfigured, hidden for eleven years, sustained by Wren and Odile. Tomas agrees to testify only if Cyrus can guarantee the ledger as corroboration. Emotional beat: the witness everyone swore was dead, alive and afraid.

chapters.title: The Safe
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Miles, POV. During the Greer family's gala, Miles opens his father's safe; Cyrus photographs the ledger, but they're caught by Aldous, who reveals he's known about Tomas for months and has been playing a longer game. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Aldous's Bargain
chapters.summary: Aldous, POV. He offers Cyrus everything—validation, position, the town's respect—in exchange for the photographs and Tomas's continued silence, revealing that Cyrus's own secret would destroy him first. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; power's final, generous-seeming corruption.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Archivist
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus refuses, burns his falsified credentials publicly before Greer can use them, and surrenders his own secret to Priya and the group—choosing truth over the belonging Greer offered. Emotional beat: catharsis; the protagonist's arc completing.

chapters.title: Day Nineteen
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. In a rushed, contested hearing, Tomas testifies, the ledger is entered, and Priya—reinstated by an outside investigator—arrests Aldous Greer as the statute expires at midnight. Emotional beat: climax; justice arriving by seconds, through many hands.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The town reckons with its complicity; some doors close to Cyrus forever. Marion Voss, alive under a new name, returns briefly to thank him and reclaim her diary. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; belonging redefined rather than restored.

chapters.title: A New Catalogue
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. He leaves the cathedral post, and the outcasts—Priya, Wren, Odile, Miles—see him off at the station, promising letters. The final image: Cyrus beginning a new archive of his own, unalphabetized, unfinished, alive. Emotional beat: hope; found family outlasting place.
